oidc_jwt.description: Valid unexpired bearer access tokens can be reused across multiple API calls and sessions.
oidc_jwt.source: RFC 6750 behavior reflected by Casdoor OAuth docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag repeated use of the same access token as replay unless the artifact is explicitly one-time.

oidc_jwt.description: Acceptance of JWTs without nbf, or lack of strict nbf enforcement, is spec-compliant because nbf is optional.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat missing nbf enforcement alone as a vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: On SSO logout, Casdoor invalidates tokens by setting ExpiresIn to 0 or a negative value, and introspection/refresh reject tokens with ExpiresIn <= 0.
oidc_jwt.note: Post-logout token rejection is expected and should not be confused with unrelated token corruption.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor issues access_token and id_token with the same JWT payload and states they can be used interchangeably.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag identical claims across access_token and id_token as token confusion by itself; this is documented behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: Using authorization_code grant with code=guest-user creates a guest account instead of completing a normal authorization-code flow.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat guest-user creation as code injection or auth bypass; it is a documented Casdoor extension.

oidc_jwt.description: For SAML upstream logins, if username mapping is absent or empty, Casdoor falls back to email and then NameID for username creation.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity derivation from email or NameID in SAML flows is documented behavior, not an unexpected merge.

oidc_jwt.description: Automatic account linking may occur by username in a case-insensitive manner when OAuth linking is enabled.
oidc_jwt.note: Case-based identity merges can be by design under configured linking behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: Admin changes to applications, providers, issuer bindings, or trusted upstream configuration are expected to take effect and authorize new behavior.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag successful auth after an admin-authorized trust/config change as a trust-anchor substitution bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Old signing keys may remain accepted until JWKS cache refresh completes after key rotation.
oidc_jwt.source: JWT/JWKS standard behavior referenced by testing guidance
oidc_jwt.note: Only flag continued acceptance after the documented/expected cache window has expired.

oidc_jwt.description: If an admin changes issuer, JWKS URL, signing key, or provider/application trust configuration, acceptance under the new trust anchor is expected.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat admin-authorized trust changes as trust-anchor substitution attacks.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor issues access_token and id_token with the same JWT payload and states they can be used interchangeably.
oidc_jwt.note: This can look suspicious to generic OIDC tooling, but is documented platform behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: With exclusive sign-in enabled, a new login removes all previous sessions for that user and application.
oidc_jwt.note: Loss of prior session after a new login is expected and should not be treated as session confusion.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Casdoor's token endpoint expects JSON request bodies in the documented examples for authorization_code, password, client_credentials, refresh_token, and token-exchange flows. Do not send form-encoded bodies unless a specific endpoint example documents form encoding; use the documented JSON shape for /api/login/oauth/access_token.

For I3 PKCE tests, if PKCE is enabled on the application, the authorization request MUST include code_challenge_method=S256 and code_challenge, and the token request MUST include the matching code_verifier. With PKCE enabled, client_secret becomes optional, but if provided it must be correct.

For I5 resource/audience binding tests, when using RFC 8707 resource indicators, the resource parameter MUST match exactly between /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. Casdoor documents exact matching; mismatches can fail for setup reasons rather than audience-validation reasons.

For I5 audience tests, Casdoor sets the access token aud claim to the resource URI when the resource parameter is supplied; otherwise aud is the client_id. The oracle must compare against the expected audience source for the specific flow.

For I2 freshness tests, application Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours. Treat value 0 for refresh token expiry as a special sentinel/default meaning immediate expiry or disabled refresh in practice for testing; do not assume refresh tokens remain usable unless RefreshExpireInHours is explicitly set to a positive value on the application.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against Casdoor as OIDC provider, include a control login using a valid token/code flow in the same setup. A failed token request can also be caused by application grant-type configuration, redirect URI mismatch, or missing PKCE parameters, not only by token freshness enforcement.

Casdoor supports bearer access tokens via Authorization: Bearer and also via query parameter accessToken on /api/userinfo. For security tests, prefer Authorization: Bearer for session-authenticated verification to avoid false positives caused by query-parameter handling differences.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, Casdoor documents that omitting scope causes the exchanged token to inherit the subject token's scope, while specifying scope is intended for narrowing. The fuzzer MUST compare requested exchanged scope against original scope and treat broader returned scope/claims as the violation condition, not mere successful exchange.

Casdoor accepts subject_token_type values access_token, jwt, and id_token for token exchange. I5 tests must vary subject_token_type explicitly; otherwise a failure may be due to unsupported token-type handling rather than audience or scope binding.

For I5 custom-scope tests, custom scopes are only available for applications with Category=Agent. Default applications expose only standard OIDC scopes. Do not request custom scopes against non-Agent applications and interpret rejection as a scope-binding bug.

For multi-tenant tests involving shared applications, a shared application's effective client_id is derived by appending -org-<organizationName>. Cross-org acceptance tests must use the organization-specific client_id variant; otherwise failures or successes may reflect shared-app routing semantics rather than audience isolation.

Casdoor application tags restrict sign-in: only users with at least one matching tag may access the application, except admins/global admins. I4/I5 tests using multiple identities must normalize or disable tag restrictions across test users, or login differences may be caused by tag gating rather than identity or authorization bugs.

If EnableExclusiveSignin is enabled on the application, a new sign-in removes all existing sessions for that user and application. I3/I4 multi-session tests must disable exclusive sign-in or isolate users, otherwise prior sessions disappearing is by design and not a session-confusion bug.

Casdoor's /api/sso-logout supports logoutAll=true by default, which deletes all active sessions for the user and expires all tokens. Cleanup or revocation tests must set logoutAll=false when they intend to preserve parallel sessions; otherwise cross-session invalidation is expected behavior.

For OIDC callback tests, RedirectUris must match exactly. Casdoor documentation repeatedly distinguishes provider callback URL (Casdoor's /callback) from application Redirect URL (the RP callback). Misconfiguring these causes authorization-code failures unrelated to security invariants.

Casdoor's token endpoint accepts JSON request bodies in the documented examples for authorization_code, password, client_credentials, refresh_token, and token_exchange. The fuzzer MUST send application/json to /api/login/oauth/access_token for these flows unless explicitly testing form-encoding compatibility.

For I3 PKCE/coherence tests, if code_challenge/code_challenge_method=S256 were sent to /login/oauth/authorize, the token request to /api/login/oauth/access_token MUST include the matching code_verifier. With PKCE enabled, client_secret is optional, but if provided it must be correct.

For RFC 8707 audience/resource tests, the resource parameter MUST match exactly between /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. Casdoor documents exact-match behavior; mismatched resource values will fail for configuration reasons rather than revealing an audience-binding bug.

For I2 freshness tests, application ExpireInHours and RefreshExpireInHours are configured in hours. The fuzzer SHOULD generate control tokens with exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and iat={{now_epoch}} semantics when validating expiry behavior, and distinguish token rejection from broken client/application configuration.

Numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout uses 0 as a sentinel meaning 'use the global default', not literal zero seconds. Never assume 0 disables waiting; it selects the platform default countdown instead.

Numeric sentinel: refresh token expiration defaults to 0 hours at the application level. Documentation states this as the default setting field value, so the fuzzer MUST NOT assume 0 means immediate expiry without confirming the effective runtime behavior for that application.

For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti tests, bearer access tokens are standard reusable bearer credentials in Casdoor. Reusing the same valid access token across multiple API calls or sessions is not evidence of a replay flaw unless a one-time artifact is being tested.

For I3 config-change sequences involving trust anchors, Casdoor supports admin-authorized provider and application reconfiguration. A login succeeding after an admin changes provider/application trust settings is BY DESIGN; only continued acceptance of old trust after the intended change should be treated as suspicious.

For OIDC callback tests, session_token MUST be the access_token, not the id_token, even though Casdoor documents that access_token and id_token are the same payload. Subsequent API calls such as /api/userinfo are documented to use the access token.

For I5 address-claim tests, token format matters: only JWT-Standard emits an OIDC-compliant address object. JWT, JWT-Empty, and JWT-Custom emit address as a raw string array. The fuzzer MUST set token format appropriately before asserting address-claim semantics.

For I4 case-confusion tests, organization setting isUsernameLowered can lowercase usernames. If enabled, case-only differences may collapse by design; the fuzzer must record this normalization setting before treating case folding as an identity-binding violation.

For I4 email/username binding tests, organizations may enable 'Use email as username'. When enabled and username is hidden at signup, email becomes the username and later email changes also update username. The fuzzer MUST treat this as configured identity derivation, not spontaneous identity collapse.

For multi-tenant tests, Casdoor resources are organization-scoped. Users belong to exactly one organization, and applications/providers are attached to organizations. The fuzzer MUST keep organization ownership consistent across application, user, and login URLs to avoid false cross-tenant results.

For shared-application tests, a shared application's effective client_id may be suffixed with -org-<organizationName>. The fuzzer MUST use the organization-specific client_id form when testing shared applications across orgs, otherwise audience/client binding results may be misinterpreted.

Casdoor's token endpoint accepts JSON request bodies in the provided docs/examples for authorization_code, password, client_credentials, refresh_token, and token-exchange grants. Use JSON for these flows unless a specific endpoint example explicitly requires form encoding; do not assume generic OAuth form encoding for /api/login/oauth/access_token on this platform.

For RFC 8707 resource-indicator tests, the resource parameter MUST match exactly between /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. If they differ, failures are expected by design and do not indicate an audience-binding bug.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a CONTROL login using a valid token flow on the same application/client configuration. A failed attack login without a successful control cannot distinguish token-validation behavior from broken application setup or disabled grant types.

Casdoor documents that access_token and id_token are the same JWT payload and can be used interchangeably. For executor behavior, session_token MUST still be mapped to access_token because subsequent API calls use Bearer access tokens; do not treat identical payloads as separate proof artifacts.

Refresh token expiration has a numeric sentinel: application Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours. In Casdoor docs, 0 means the platform default configuration value, not necessarily literal immediate expiry. Never assume 0 disables refresh or means zero lifetime without confirming the application setting.

Code resend timeout has a numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout value 0 means use the global default, not literal zero seconds. Never assume 0 disables throttling or allows immediate resend.

Cookie/session expiration has a numeric sentinel: CookieExpireInHours value 0 means use the default session cookie lifetime, not literal zero hours. Do not use 0 in tests expecting immediate session expiry.

For I3 config-change tests involving application settings (grant types, redirect URIs, token format, exclusive sign-in, tags, org choice mode), admin-authorized changes taking effect for NEW logins are by design. A valid coherence test must show inconsistent handling of the same request under unchanged config, not merely that an admin changed behavior.

For PKCE-related OIDC tests, when PKCE is enabled Casdoor requires code_verifier on token exchange; client_secret becomes optional, but if provided it must be correct. Do not interpret rejection of a wrong client_secret during PKCE as a PKCE bug.

For OIDC authorization-code clients such as Claude Desktop/Cursor-style native apps, redirect URI matching is exact except that Casdoor documentation explicitly allows wildcard localhost ports in configured Redirect URIs for those clients. Tests using localhost callback wildcards must configure the application accordingly; otherwise redirect_uri mismatch is expected.

For I5 scope-escalation tests on token exchange, Casdoor documents that omitting scope causes the new token to inherit the subject token's scope, while specifying scope is intended for narrowing to a subset. A valid escalation test must request a STRICT SUPERSET of the original scope and verify whether extra claims/permissions appear; requesting no scope is not an escalation attempt.

For I5 audience-binding tests, when the authorization request includes resource, Casdoor sets the resulting access token aud claim to the resource URI instead of the client_id. Test oracles must compare aud against the configured resource URI in that case, not against client_id.

Casdoor's /api/userinfo response is scope-dependent and may return only basic claims such as sub/iss/aud unless additional scopes were requested at token issuance. For I4/I5 verification, request the needed scopes during login; missing claims in /api/userinfo are not evidence of stripping or authorization bugs.

For multi-tenant/shared-application tests, shared applications use an org-specific suffix in client_id/application reference: -org-<organizationName>. Cross-org behavior must be tested with the suffixed client identifier; using the base shared client_id without the org suffix can produce misleading routing or tenant-binding results.

Casdoor supports automatic account linking for OAuth logins by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitively. For I4 collision tests involving upstream OAuth/OIDC providers, account merges based on configured linking are by design and must not be flagged unless the merge exceeds the documented linking policy.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: A pre-configured test environment exists: organization 'test-org', application 'app-test' (query clientId/clientSecret via GET /api/get-application?id=admin/app-test), and SAML provider 'provider-saml-test' already linked to app-test. For MOST tests, REUSE these resources instead of creating new ones. Only create new organizations/applications when the attack specifically requires distinct tenants (e.g., I5 cross-org token exchange). OWNERSHIP RULES: Applications and providers MUST use owner='admin'. Users MUST use owner=<organization_name> (e.g., 'test-org'). NEVER use 'built-in' as organization for create_user — the built-in org forbids user creation. GRANT TYPES: When creating applications, ALWAYS include grantTypes=['password','authorization_code','urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange'] and enablePassword=true and cert='cert-built-in' unless the test specifically requires otherwise. MULTI-APP SEQUENCES: When a test needs two separate applications (e.g., token exchange between different clients/audiences), use 'app-test' as the SOURCE application (already exists) and create ONE new application as the TARGET. Create users with signupApplication matching the app they will login to. For login_with_password, the executor auto-resolves client_id from the user's signupApplication — so set signupApplication correctly in create_user.
